findings.comment: Repeat Violation
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments. Two live adults were observed under counters in the cook line and service line. One adult was observed fast-moving under the left side of the cook line. The other adult was observed live on a glue trap under a service line counter. The right side of the cook line near the grill and fryers used to be the focal point of pest presence, but no pests were observed in this area today. Glue traps were observed placed throughout the cook line and service line. SCDPH will continue to follow-up until no pests are observed. This means keeping the glue traps present as a monitoring tool and insuring treatment is curtailing life cycles. The next follow-up is scheduled for September 28, 2026.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 CK and EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. New technician has been secured from Terminex. The facility has date-marked glue traps throughout the facility to help monitor the presence of pests. These glue traps were dated from 1/2/26, many of them were nearly empty. 
Keep working to seal gaps in walls. There are areas around the cookline preparation cooler where wall trim is pulling from wall. Work to keep the walls sealed tight and to prevent movement of the pests from one part of the kitchen to another. 
Keep cleaning, keep working to eliminate moisture, and keep cardboard out of the kitchen (switch to plastic totes as you’re able). 
When you pull-out equipment for cleaning, look at removing the backs of various pieces of equipment that may house roaches. Have the inside of equipment serviced for pests.
The facility will continue to be monitored on a 30 day rotation until no pests are observed in the glue traps. Multiple roaches observed in glue traps, one slow moving nymph behind the cookline preparation cooler and one fast moving adult behind the same cooler. 



 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed 5 live, fast-moving roaches, 1 live, slow-moving roach, and 1 dead roach in the facility. The PIC stated that the last pest control visit was 12/16. The visits are bi-weekly. There were no glue traps observed placed throughout the facility. The PIC claims that another employee has been removing the glue traps. Ensure dated glue traps are placed throughout the dining room, bathrooms, service line, kitchen, dish room, and dry storage areas. Ensure that cardboard is removed from areas where pest concerns are known, as cardboard can both harbor and feed pests. Clean areas (especially drains) as frequently as possible to reduce food and water sources. A follow-up will be conducted on January 14, 2026 to ensure the presence of pests in the facility is declining. 

***Ensure receipts are kept in facility for all pest control visits***

findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival there was not a CFPM at the facility. A CFPM arrived during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that there are enough CFPMS to cover all shifts.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

Multiple cleaned plans in the kitchen area are observed with minor food debris still on them. They are stored as ready for use. The PIC was shown and moved the dishes back to the dish area for re-cleaning. Ensure that all dishes are completely clean prior to storage.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-202.12: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be used according to LAW(C), Manufacturer’s directions (indicate for use in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT) (P), conditions of certification (if applicable) (P), and additional conditions (if applicable) (C). (B) POISIONOUS MATERIALS shall be applied so HAZARD is not constituted to individuals and contamination from chemical is prevented (P).

A sani bucket was in the process of being reset as the inspection began. The chemical used to fill the bucket by the employee in the kitchen is the peroxide disinfectant used on tables, and is not intended for use in the kitchen. Education was conducted and the bucket was remade with the Lactic Acid sanitizer used in the facility for food contact surface sanitizing. Ensure the correct chemicals are used for the purposes that they are intended at all times.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two containers of ham were in the WIC and past the 7 day maximum.  Discussed with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure all items are discarded after the 7 day maximum allowance.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cooler at far end of cook line was holding a temperature of at least 55 degrees, 60 in other places. A container of individually prepared mashed potatoes and a container of individually prepared gravy were both probed at 50 degrees. Employees stated that it had been there since at least 6am, when pulled out of walk-in cooler. Items were voluntarily discarded and fridge was marked out of order.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Knife used for slicing food stored in a soiled sanitizer bucket. Bucket was dumped and replaced. Education provided on proper storage of utensils. Acceptable options include: on cutting surfaces and cleaned every 4 hours or between rushes, stored on stovetop where heat will kill pathogens. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.11: (A) Multiuse FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be smooth, free of breaks, cracks, sharp angles, and finished to have SMOOTH welds and joints. Also, it shall be accessible for cleaning and inspection with easy disassembling. 

All cutting board, food staging surfaces at edge of grills/stoves warped by heat and marked with deep knife grooves. Items are no longer smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

All CFMs must have completed allergen awareness training by next routine inspection. Facility recently moved to a high risk and now allergen training is required of all CFMs under the high risk permit class. Signage for allergen awareness posted behind register.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the risks inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation.
-PIC observed improperly washing hands, consuming/storing beverages in prep area, and using cell phone in food prep areas. 
-PIC unable to correctly answer questions related to proper sanitizer use, labeling, and test strips for specific chemicals. 

These items were addressed with PIC at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. 

Observed PIC drinking an energy drink in the food preparation area. All personal drinks must be stored and drank in a designated space away from food-prep areas to prevent spillage and accidental contamination. Discussed with PIC. Corrected on site.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

Observed PIC use bare hands to shut off faucet of handsink in cook line. Discussed with PIC. After drying hands with disposable towel, the sink should be shut off using the towel to avoid re-contamination of hands.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems.

Several food items have expired use by dates. These items include: Turkey gravy individually portioned (9/7), corn kernels individually portioned (9/7), and chicken tenders (9/6). These items were voluntarily discarded by PIC at time of inspection. 

Also, PIC reported that the datemarking machine failed yesterday evening, so some prepped items have a handwritten datemark with a label indicating how many days the item is good for (ie. 4 days). Discussed with PIC this is not an adequate date label as we do not know the reference date from which the time starts from. Discussed need for a standardized date labeling system. PIC relabeled these items with 9/12 as a discard date to keep with standard datemarking system IHOP utilizes.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.
7-204.11: (A)-(B): Chemical SANITIZERS applied for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall meet regulatory requirements.

Working bottles of peroxide sanitizer for tables, taken from a larger container, are not labeled. Discussed with PIC that all spray bottles must be labeled with the main chemical components. Additionally, labeling on bulk container of peroxide lacks labeling specifying pathogen destruction and directions for ppm use and use on food contact surfaces. 

PIC opted to cease use of these chemicals until proper labeling (and test strips in violation #48) can be obtained by manufacturer (Ecolab).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips for peroxide sanitizer not available. See violation #28. Cease use of this chemical until proper requirements are met.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
6-202.110: Outdoor REFUSE areas shall be constructed in accordance with LAW and shall be curbed and graded to drain to collect and dispose of liquid waste that results from the REFUSE and from cleaning the area and waste receptacles.
5-501.110: REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be stored in receptacles or waste handling units so that they are inaccessible to insects and rodents.

Facility has 2 sets of dumpsters, one from Republic and one from Waste Management. PIC stated the Republic is an old utility and are set to be picked up within the week. The in-use dumpsters from Waste Management are placed outside the dumpster enclosure in the parking lot. These dumpsters are observed leaking onto the pavement and full. Discussed proper storage of outdoor waste recepticles.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. (REPEAT)
The following surfaces are in need of repair: 1) Caulking around handsink in dish area 2) tiles in walk-in cooler flooring 3)tiles in dining room with signs of water damage. 

Discussed with PIC. Stated they are working on removing tile in walk-in and sealing it off. Will follow up at next routine. Stated that the roof did have a leaking issues, which was fixed with re-rubbering. There is an outstanding estimate/bid for repair work to occur in ceiling now that leak is fixed. This is managed by upper-management at IHOP and not on-site management.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11: ((B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

Ensure employee personal items (drinks and cell phones observed at today's inspection) are kept in a designated area away from food prep surfaces. Calls and texts should be answered in this designated area and employee should complete a proper handwash prior to returning to work. Discussed with PIC.
